input:
This passage reports a shell-and-tube heat exchanger used to heat crude oil within a refinery preheat train, the sequence of exchangers through which crude oil passes to raise its temperature before the downstream processing units. The duty of the exchanger, the rate at which heat is transferred from the hot stream to the crude oil, is 561 kW. The hot stream enters the exchanger at a temperature of 150 °C and leaves it at 110 °C, while the crude oil itself enters at 35 °C and leaves at the somewhat higher temperature of 50 °C, having been heated as required.

The log-mean temperature difference for the exchanger, the appropriately averaged driving force for heat transfer along the unit, allowing for the way the local temperature difference varies from one end to the other, is 86.9 K. The installed heat-transfer area is 24.4 m2, and when the duty, the area and the log-mean temperature difference are combined together, they yield an overall heat-transfer coefficient of 265 W m-2 K-1. This overall coefficient bundles the thermal resistances of the films on both sides of the tubes with the resistance of the tube wall itself, all expressed with reference to the installed area, and it characterises this particular exchanger at this particular duty, rather than describing either stream in isolation.

Finally, the question of fouling deserves mention. Fouling was assessed on the basis of a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has yet been completed on the exchanger. This means that the assessment reflects only the fouled condition that happened to prevail during that one run: the reported coefficient is the value for a fouled exchanger at some unrecorded point between cleanings, and there is no clean-surface coefficient available against which it might meaningfully be compared. Both the performance that would be obtained immediately after cleaning and the rate at which fouling would build up again afterwards remain unmeasured.
target:
A shell-and-tube exchanger in a refinery preheat train heats crude oil at a duty of 561 kW. Duty is the heat transferred per unit time, and the preheat train is the sequence of exchangers that raises the crude oil temperature before downstream processing. The hot stream enters at 150 °C and leaves at 110 °C; the crude oil enters at 35 °C and leaves at 50 °C. The log-mean temperature difference for the exchanger is 86.9 K, the installed area is 24.4 m2, and the overall coefficient that follows from duty, area and log-mean difference together is 265 W m-2 K-1.

The log-mean temperature difference is the mean driving force for heat transfer along the exchanger, formed from the terminal differences so that the fall in driving force from end to end is correctly weighted. The overall coefficient bundles the resistances of the two films and the wall into a single figure referred to the installed area, so the value describes this exchanger at this duty rather than either stream on its own. The modest rise of the crude oil against the larger fall of the hot stream reflects the balance of the two heat-capacity rates at the stated duty, with the same heat quantity carried on both sides of the wall.

Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run. No cleaning cycle has been completed, so the assessment holds the fouling state of that run only: the coefficient is the value for a fouled exchanger at an unrecorded point between cleanings, and no clean-surface coefficient is available for comparison. Performance after cleaning, and the rate at which fouling returns, are both unmeasured, and the exchanger stands reported at its fouled condition.
